newsitem.title: USA: Restrictions eased on Mississippi at New Orleans.
newsitem.headline: Restrictions eased on Mississippi at New Orleans.

text.p: Mississippi River traffic at New Orleans was gradually being restored to normal, although shipping still was allowed only one-way at a time following a weekend freighter accident, the Coast Guard said Thursday.

Maritime traffic has been curtailed on the lower Mississippi River since Saturday, when a grain freighter, the Bright Field, ploughed into a waterfront shopping centre near the heart of downtown New Orleans. More than 100 people were injured in the accident, but no one was killed.

The Coast Guard said it raised the draft limit on vessels navigating through the Port of New Orleans to 46 feet. But some shipping restrictions remained in place, Coast Guard officials said, including a ban on simultaneous two-way traffic at the port.

"Right now the river is open to traffic up to 46 feet," said Lt. Curtis Shaw, of the Coast Guard's Marine Safety Office in New Orleans. "(Traffic) is in-bound and out-bound, but it is one way at a time," he added.
With the port open to all but the largest tankers, officials said there were no vessels waiting to enter or leave the river late Thursday.
The wharf was heavily damaged in the collision, and the freighter, which was thought to be supporting part of the structure, was being held in place by tugboats.
